A Great Indie multiplayer game to play with friends

 I have low hours on my account but I have been playing with family and friends on their accounts. Its the best aliens game that never was, very difficult and incredibly fun multiplayer not really a solo game, you can play by yourself I wouldn't advise it. The game takes a lot of inspiration from the aliens movie the machine gun sound and muzzle flare are dead ringers. You have up to four players doing certain missions on ships, rescue or destroy, the levels start out dim in pitch blackness with only your flashlight and weapon of your choosing with limited battery and it quickly become tense and frantic when the aliens arrive, fast moving and dangerous killing you in seconds. The game makes you tigger happy and may result in you shooting your comrades by accident. 
The game has a learning curve, much of the game has you going to blue terminals and hacking them, you have to wait for the numbers to reach 100% you have to find all of them to finish a level. This sounds boring but its intentional like I said there are aliens coming through walls and vents, so sitting around in an area where they are waiting is its own kind of tension. Finishing terminals give you upgrades for your character and everyone else, this game has rogue like elements so the upgrades are random, from a faster hacking speed, nightvision, faster movement, brighter flashlight, increased ammo capacity ect. However this is important if you die you lose your upgrades so play well. The other two terminals you will find are repair stations in case you do survive being mauled, and ammo recharge stations cause you will go through ammo like crazy especially if there are multiple breaches. You can also upgrade if you survive the mission to the end and it allows you to rank up giving you better ammo types. These are perminant between missions however (at least to my knowledge) once you exit the game you start back to square one which I wish they let you keep between sessions.
Finally teamwork is important. Some levels are absolutly massive and maze like, in some there is a map room, so one guy can stay there giving directions to the others, your not just equipped with a gun, you can hack turrets and activate lazer grids to help with the swarm. So one player can hack the blue terminals providing upgrades, one can activate turrets and keep the swarm at bay, while one is in the map room giving directions. Though this game is a rogue like and if you rely on the turrets the aliens will knock out the power leaving you in the dark, (this is how you start each level as well) to reactivate it you must find a junction box. While I praise the rogue like elements soimetimes it can be a pain, sometimes a break in area will be right in the map room or in the reactor where you need to finish some levels. 
 This is one of the best multiplayer local co-op games to play with friends, I have already sank 50hrs on the game and comes recommended.

It's a fun game to just hop into, play a few rounds, then dip out. It's got some progression stuff here and there if you're interested in taking runs as far as you can, but overall it's a VERY simple game. It feels like the game is trying to make you have sensory overload simply to hide how simple the game really is.

Missions go as such:
[*] Get in
[*] Hit datacores
[*] Leave
[*] Shoot aliens on the way

There are 2 alien types, so the challenge really comes in the form of the procedural maps and pure enemy numbers. Sometimes they're tough, sometimes they're easy, just depends on what the game gives you. Game really doesn't get any more complex than that. You're not really making a lot of decisions, just trying to do your job as fast as possible so you don't get overwhelmed.

The feeling of IMMENSE pressure you feel while playing the game is pretty intense. I really enjoyed how suddenly things could go from 0 to 100 in an instant. You really feel like you're the prey and NOT the ones in control - assuming there's not like 30 sentries and laser gates. 

My only primary issues with the game so far are the extreme [b]SENSORY OVERLOAD[/b]. From your gun literally blinding you, to the fov changing based on alien proximity (do yourself a favor and turn both of these off in the options, oml) you are constantly just trying to catch your bearings. Did you kill an alien? No idea, just keep spraying and praying until beeps, boops, and alien screams stop (great feeling tbh, until you get auto aim). Is that a friendly in front of you? The game will [i]let you know[/i] with nice big FLASHING "friendly!!!" text that blocks your vision. I'm torn between loving the way it's put together and absolutely hating some of the things - the friendly text should just be a green crosshair, for example. I genuinely think that with a second pass on a lot of this hud stuff that it could be equally overloading while also being a bit less obtrusive. 

There [i]is[/i] an upgrade system in the game, but how much it affects you depends on the type of run you're doing in-game. If you die in multiplayer and revive you also lose all your upgrades. The upgrades are mostly just helpful things (map markers, waypoint guidance, etc) and strict ammo counts/interact speed type upgrades. You definitely miss them when you don't have them, but it's not a terribly deep or complex system.

If any of this sounds interesting, you'd probably like the game enough on a sale. This game is a fun time for sure, but I could definitely see it getting old quick if you catch onto the systems quick and aren't interested in 0 meta progression.

Con más de 50 horas de juego en Space Beast Terror Fright, puedo decir que este título ofrece una experiencia única y llena de adrenalina. El juego captura el terror y la tensión de enfrentarse a lo desconocido en espacios claustrofóbicos y oscuros, lo cual lo convierte en una opción ideal para quienes buscan una mezcla de acción y horror en primera persona. Desde la primera misión, SBTF logra hacer que el jugador sienta una intensa presión en cada movimiento y decisión.

Puntos positivos:

- Tensión constante: La atmósfera del juego es increíblemente tensa y te mantiene en el borde del asiento. La combinación de oscuridad, sonidos inquietantes y enemigos implacables crea un nivel de suspenso poco común.

- Jugabilidad en equipo: El modo cooperativo hace que cada partida sea única. Coordinarse con otros jugadores para explorar, hackear y sobrevivir hace que la experiencia sea intensa y gratificante.

- Mapas generados proceduralmente: La generación aleatoria de mapas hace que cada partida sea distinta, manteniendo la experiencia fresca y asegurando que cada incursión sea un desafío nuevo.

- Dificultad desafiante: El juego no es fácil y te hace trabajar por cada victoria. La dificultad elevada añade valor de rejugabilidad para quienes buscan mejorar sus habilidades y estrategias.

- Minimalismo eficaz: Aunque el juego tiene un diseño gráfico sencillo, utiliza bien los elementos visuales y de sonido para crear una experiencia inmersiva y aterradora.

Puntos negativos:

- Curva de aprendizaje empinada: Al principio, puede ser abrumador para nuevos jugadores, ya que el juego no ofrece mucha ayuda o tutoriales, lo que puede frustrar a quienes recién comienzan.

- Gráficos limitados: Aunque el minimalismo tiene su atractivo, los gráficos pueden sentirse un poco anticuados, especialmente para quienes están acostumbrados a visuales más modernos.

- Poca variedad de enemigos: La falta de diversidad en los enemigos puede hacer que el juego se sienta repetitivo después de muchas horas, y sería interesante ver más tipos de amenazas.

- Dependencia de compañeros de equipo: El juego es mucho mejor en cooperativo, y jugar en solitario no es tan atractivo o efectivo. Esto puede ser una limitación para quienes prefieren experiencias individuales.

- Escasa progresión o desbloqueos: No hay mucha progresión en términos de desbloqueos o mejoras, lo que puede hacer que la experiencia de juego se estanque a largo plazo.

Resumen final:

Space Beast Terror Fright es una recomendación segura para los amantes de la acción y el horror cooperativo. La tensión y el reto de sobrevivir en sus oscuros laberintos, combinado con el caos de la colaboración en tiempo real, hacen que cada partida sea una experiencia intensa. Aunque hay aspectos que podrían mejorar, como la variedad de enemigos o un sistema de progresión más robusto, sigue siendo una experiencia única y llena de adrenalina que merece la pena explorar.
